Yes, Champagne comes solely from the Champagne region of France. [d1] According to Wikipedia, "many legal structures reserve the word Champagne exclusively for sparkling wines from the Champagne region," with over 70 countries legally protecting this designation under international treaties. [d2] As Total Wine states plainly: "Only sparkling wine from the Champagne region of France is Champagne. Everything else is sparkling wine." [d5] This is echoed by wine.co.za, which notes that "Champagne comes solely from the Champagne region of northeastern France," where it is made using the labor-intensive méthode Champenoise. [d7] The legal dimension is further confirmed by the fact that "the term Champagne can solely be used if the wine comes from this region only," and [d8] you "cannot legally call that wonderful bubbly drink 'champagne' unless it comes from the Champagne region of France." [d3] In short, every bottle of real Champagne comes from Champagne, France — if it doesn't come from the designated Champagne region, it is not Champagne, regardless of how similar it may taste.
